heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

SOUTH TANGERANG CITY

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this regional regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Mayor, and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government of South Tangerang City.
2. Mayor is the Mayor of South Tangerang.
3. Implementation is the form of execution of protection for women and child victims of violence.
4. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who has obtained legal status as a Woman.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
11. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an institution that provides services and protection for women and children especially those who have problems due to acts of violence, discrimination, human trafficking and other social problems in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social, public facility services and legal protection and assistance.
16. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other Community Organizations.
17. Resident is a South Tangerang Citizen and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the South Tangerang City area.
18. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
19. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery for victims of violence as stipulated in a decision of an authorized official.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance for the self-strengthening of victims of violence, especially victims of domestic violence, to resolve the problems they face.
21. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that carries out integrated service functions for women and child victims of violence, based on hospitals, Community Health Centers, P2TP2A and other similar institutions that are managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of women's and children's human rights and the best interests of victims.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
translated_text:
Article 3

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence aims to provide prevention, protection, and services for women and children against gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in the household or public.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
translated_text:
Article 4

The prevention activities against the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3, include:
a. Socialization;
b. Dissemination; and
c. Training.

heading: Article 5
heading_path: CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

heading: CHAPTER III
CHAPTER IV
Article 8
heading_path: CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
translated_text:
Article 8

In carrying out its obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 7, the Regional Government must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, wives or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 9

1. In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.
2. The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements from the Regional Government and elements from related institutions outside the Regional Government.
3. Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.
4. The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with institutions and or organizations in South Tangerang City and other regions.
5. In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, Integrated Service Posts may be established at the sub-district and urban village levels.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

HANDLING AND MECHANISM

Article 10

1. The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
2. The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
3. Principles of Service and Assistance:
a. Fast, safe and empathetic;
b. Guarantee of confidentiality;
c. Easily accessible;
d. Free of charge.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION

Article 11

1. Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
2. Forms of physical violence include any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
3. Forms of sexual violence include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
4. Forms of economic violence include neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
5. Forms of psychological violence include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 12
heading_path: CHAPTER VII
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
translated_text:
Article 12

1. Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
2. Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be provided to residents of South Tangerang City whether committed in South Tangerang City or outside South Tangerang City.
3. Protection for women and children victims of violence as an initial action shall also be provided to non-residents of South Tangerang City where the incident occurred within the territory of South Tangerang City, followed by coordination with the region of origin of such residents.

heading: Article 13
heading_path: CHAPTER VII
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
translated_text:
Article 13

1. Forms of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
2. Forms of medical protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), include treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
3. Forms of legal protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), include services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
4. Forms of medicolegal protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), include medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
5. Forms of psychological protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), include assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
6. Forms of economic protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), include services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 14

1. The Regional Government in implementing the protection of Women and Children Victims of violence, may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

heading: Article 15
heading_path: CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
translated_text:
Article 15

1. Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the Regional Government through Regional Work Units related to the task of protection and empowerment of women and children.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may include social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

SOURCES OF FUNDS AND REPORTING

Article 16

1. Sources of funds for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence carried out by regional apparatus of South Tangerang City shall come from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Tangerang City.
2. Sources of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legitimate and non-binding sources.
3. Sources of funds for implementation from other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be supervised in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. The PPT is obligated to report the implementation of protection activities for women and children victims of violence periodically to the Mayor in accordance with applicable regulations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

PROVISIONS ON SANCTIONS

Article 17

1. Institutions or bodies designated by the Mayor to carry out service tasks that violate the principles of service as stated in Article 10 paragraph (3), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Perpetrators of acts of violence shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with applicable Laws.
3. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 18

This Regional Regulation shall come into force from the date of its enactment.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of South Tangerang City.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY

NUMBER 3 OF 2012 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute a violation of human rights and a crime against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, as amended. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honour, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence and domestic neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence, particularly domestic violence. Legal reform that favours vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, has become very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence; this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 the number of violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totalled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police of Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011, 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police of Tangerang Regency; this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence, especially those occurring within the household, are still considered a disgrace in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be owned by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions, whether legal, political, economic or social, to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In carrying out the guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of the community is needed, whether through women's and children's protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, the business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code as amended, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counsellors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, the Agency or Office that has duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implements preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 2

The rights in this provision are intended to guarantee their lives in accordance with human dignity, increase self-confidence, and the ability to participate in community, national, and state life. What is meant by discriminatory treatment, for example, is treatment that differentiates ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status, birth order of children, and physical and/or mental condition.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a state in which women and men enjoy equal status and have the same conditions to fully realize their basic rights and potential for the integrity and continuity of life proportionally.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 3

What is meant by prevention is all activities carried out to prevent, reduce and even eliminate acts of violence, among others, by organizing communication, information and education. What is meant by services and protection for women and children victims of gender-based violence is that in all service and protection actions, gender equality is taken into account. What is meant by the best interests of the child is that in all actions concerning children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by socialization is a process of instilling or transferring habits or values and rules from one generation to another generation in a group or society regarding the prevention of violence.

Letter b
What is meant by dissemination is an activity aimed at target groups or individuals so that they obtain information, awareness arises, accept, and ultimately utilize that information.

Letter c
What is meant by Training is a series of activities designed to improve the skills, knowledge, experience, or change the attitude of an individual. Training relates to the acquisition of certain skills or knowledge. Socialization, dissemination and training activities on violence prevention can be carried out by related Regional Work Units, related Agencies, individuals, groups or Social Community Organizations.

heading: Article 5
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Letter b
What is meant by receiving psychological assistance is assistance provided by a psychologist to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. Meanwhile, legal assistance is an aid effort provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.

Letter c
What is meant by counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert or a person trained in such a way that the victim's psychological understanding and ability increases in solving the problems faced.

Letter d
What is meant by spiritual guidance is counseling provided by a cleric.

Letter e
What is meant by resocialization is that the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.

Letter f
What is meant by empowerment is Empowerment means making something become empowered or have power or have strength.

heading: Article 6
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH TANGERANG CITY
translated_text:
Article 6

Letter a
What is meant by Protection is that the victim receives protection from family, police, prosecution, court, advocate social institutions or other parties, either temporarily or based on a protection order from the court.

Letter b
What is meant by receiving information is the victim's right to obtain information related to prevention, complaints, medical services and protection.

Letter c
What is meant by Optimal service is service that can be provided to victims in accordance with the capacity of those providing it.

Letter d
What is meant by Continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage is handling provided up to the recovery of the victim in society.

Letter e
What is meant by confidential handling is an effort to guarantee certainty for the victim that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Letter f
What is meant by Psychological and legal assistance is the victim's right to receive psychological and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Letter g
What is meant by Guarantee of rights related to status as a family member and member of society.
